paragraphs.title: The Final Plague and Israel’s Expulsion

easy.question: To whom did the Lord say these words in the verse?
answers: Moses
Pharaoh
Aaron
easy.explanation: The verse begins, “And the Lord said unto Moses.”

easy.question: How many more plagues did the Lord say He would bring upon Pharaoh and Egypt?
answers: Three
One
Two
easy.explanation: The Lord said, “Yet will I bring one plague more.”

easy.question: What would Pharaoh do after the final plague?
answers: Ask Moses to stay
Bless Israel
Send the Israelites out of Egypt
easy.explanation: The Lord said that afterward Pharaoh would “let you go hence.”

medium.question: What does the phrase “one plague more” indicate?
answers: A punishment or blow
A gift
A journey
medium.explanation: The phrase describes another punishment that the Lord would bring upon Pharaoh and Egypt.

medium.question: What would happen after the Lord brought the final plague?
answers: Moses would return to Midian
Pharaoh would send the Israelites out
Egypt would ask Moses to lead it
medium.explanation: The verse connects the final plague with the result: Pharaoh would let the Israelites go.

medium.question: What does the phrase “thrust you out hence altogether” emphasize?
answers: Pharaoh would change his mind immediately
The Israelites would remain in Egypt
Pharaoh would force the Israelites to leave
medium.explanation: The phrase shows that Pharaoh would not merely permit them to leave; he would drive them out completely.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the word “Yet” at the beginning of the verse?
answers: There had already been earlier plagues
This was the first plague
The plague would come a year later
challenge.explanation: “Yet” shows that this plague would come in addition to the plagues that had already occurred.

challenge.question: What sequence of events is described in the verse?
answers: Pharaoh drives out Israel, and then the plague comes
Another plague comes, and then Pharaoh sends out and drives out Israel
Israel returns to Egypt, and then Pharaoh sends them away
challenge.explanation: The verse presents the plague first, followed by Pharaoh sending out and driving away the Israelites.

challenge.question: What is emphasized by “let you go hence” and “thrust you out hence altogether”?
answers: The Israelites would move to another city in Egypt
Pharaoh would send only Moses
The Israelites would leave Egypt and not remain there
challenge.explanation: Both phrases emphasize leaving the place—in other words, leaving Egypt and ending their stay there.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the word “Yet” at the beginning of the verse?
answers: There had already been earlier plagues
This was the first plague
The plague would come a year later
questions.explanation: “Yet” shows that this plague would come in addition to the plagues that had already occurred.

questions.question: What sequence of events is described in the verse?
answers: Pharaoh drives out Israel, and then the plague comes
Another plague comes, and then Pharaoh sends out and drives out Israel
Israel returns to Egypt, and then Pharaoh sends them away
questions.explanation: The verse presents the plague first, followed by Pharaoh sending out and driving away the Israelites.

questions.question: What is emphasized by “let you go hence” and “thrust you out hence altogether”?
answers: The Israelites would move to another city in Egypt
Pharaoh would send only Moses
The Israelites would leave Egypt and not remain there
questions.explanation: Both phrases emphasize leaving the place—in other words, leaving Egypt and ending their stay there.

paragraphs.title: Silver and Gold and Favor in the Egyptians’ Sight

easy.question: What were the people told to ask from the Egyptians?
answers: Silver and gold jewelry
Clothes and horses
Bread and water
easy.explanation: The people were told to ask the Egyptians for silver and gold jewelry.

easy.question: From whom was each man to ask?
answers: Pharaoh
His neighbor
Moses
easy.explanation: The verse says, “let every man borrow of his neighbour.”

easy.question: In whose sight was Moses very great?
answers: In the sight of the Israelites only
In Pharaoh’s sight only
In the sight of Pharaoh’s servants and the people
easy.explanation: The verse says that Moses was very great in the sight of Pharaoh’s servants and the people.

medium.question: What caused the Egyptians to agree to give the people silver and gold?
answers: The Lord gave the people favor in the Egyptians’ sight
Moses bought them with money
Pharaoh ordered them to pay a tax
medium.explanation: The verse connects the people’s favor in the Egyptians’ sight with their ability to ask the Egyptians for valuables.

medium.question: In the phrase “the Lord gave the people favour in the sight of the Egyptians,” what does “favour” mean?
answers: Physical beauty only
Goodwill and acceptance
Great fear
medium.explanation: Here, “favour” means goodwill from the Egyptians, which led them to agree to give the people valuables.

medium.question: How does the passage describe the treatment of Moses compared with the people?
answers: The people found favor, and Moses was considered very great
Moses found favor, but the people were rejected
Both the people and Moses feared the Egyptians
medium.explanation: The passage says that the Lord gave the people favor, and that Moses was also very great in the Egyptians’ sight.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the women asking their female neighbors and the men asking their male neighbors?
answers: Each person approached a familiar person of the same sex
Only the women received gold jewelry
The men were forbidden to speak with Egyptians
challenge.explanation: The wording describes personal requests between familiar people of the same sex.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “Moreover the man Moses” emphasize?
answers: Moses was great only in the people’s sight
Not only the people, but Moses too had an honored status among the Egyptians
Moses was one of Pharaoh’s servants
challenge.explanation: “Moreover” adds Moses to the description: not only the people, but Moses also was regarded as very great.

challenge.question: What sequence is described in these verses?
answers: First the Egyptians gave the valuables, and afterward the people found favor
First Moses became great, and afterward the Lord spoke to the people
First the people were told to ask for valuables, while the passage also explains that the Lord gave them favor
challenge.explanation: Verse 2 gives the instruction to ask for silver and gold, while verse 3 explains the favor and status that supported this request.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the women asking their female neighbors and the men asking their male neighbors?
answers: Each person approached a familiar person of the same sex
Only the women received gold jewelry
The men were forbidden to speak with Egyptians
questions.explanation: The wording describes personal requests between familiar people of the same sex.

questions.question: What does the phrase “Moreover the man Moses” emphasize?
answers: Moses was great only in the people’s sight
Not only the people, but Moses too had an honored status among the Egyptians
Moses was one of Pharaoh’s servants
questions.explanation: “Moreover” adds Moses to the description: not only the people, but Moses also was regarded as very great.

questions.question: What sequence is described in these verses?
answers: First the Egyptians gave the valuables, and afterward the people found favor
First Moses became great, and afterward the Lord spoke to the people
First the people were told to ask for valuables, while the passage also explains that the Lord gave them favor
questions.explanation: Verse 2 gives the instruction to ask for silver and gold, while verse 3 explains the favor and status that supported this request.

paragraphs.title: The Death of the Firstborn and the Distinction Between the Peoples

easy.question: When would the Lord go out through the midst of Egypt?
answers: At midnight
In the morning
Toward evening
easy.explanation: The verse says, “About midnight will I go out into the midst of Egypt.”

easy.question: Who would die in the plague of the firstborn?
answers: Only Pharaoh’s firstborn
Every firstborn in Egypt, including the firstborn of animals
Only the firstborn of servants
easy.explanation: The passage describes the death of every firstborn, from Pharaoh’s firstborn to the firstborn of the maidservant, as well as the firstborn of animals.

easy.question: What would not happen to the Israelites?
answers: They would have no food
They would be unable to leave their homes
Not even a dog would move its tongue against them
easy.explanation: The passage says that among the Israelites not even a dog would move its tongue.

medium.question: What would happen as a result of the death of the firstborn in Egypt?
answers: A great cry would be heard throughout Egypt
The Egyptians would celebrate
The Israelites would return to Egypt
medium.explanation: The death of the firstborn would cause a great cry throughout the land of Egypt.

medium.question: What does the phrase “not a dog move his tongue” mean in context?
answers: The dogs would run away
The dogs would not bark or make a sound
The dogs would attack the Egyptians
medium.explanation: In context, the phrase means that not even the sound of a dog would be heard among the Israelites.

medium.question: Why is the difference between Egypt and Israel emphasized?
answers: So that the Israelites would remain in Egypt
So that the Egyptians would learn to speak Hebrew
So that the Israelites would know that the Lord distinguishes between Egypt and Israel
medium.explanation: The verse explicitly says that this distinction would show the Israelites that the Lord separates them from the Egyptians.

challenge.question: What does the detail “from the firstborn of Pharaoh ... even unto the firstborn of the maidservant” teach?
answers: The plague would affect every social class, from the king to the maidservant
The plague would affect only Pharaoh’s family
The plague would affect only slaves
challenge.explanation: The range from Pharaoh to the maidservant emphasizes that every social class in Egypt would be affected.

challenge.question: Who is speaking in the words “will I go out into the midst of Egypt”?
answers: Moses
The Lord
Pharaoh
challenge.explanation: Moses introduces the message with “Thus saith the Lord,” so “I” refers to the Lord.

challenge.question: What is the meaning of the statement “such as there was none like it, nor shall be like it any more”?
answers: The cry would last only a short time
The cry would be heard only in villages
It would be an unprecedented and never-repeated cry
challenge.explanation: The repeated comparison emphasizes the extraordinary, unprecedented nature of the event.

questions.question: What does the detail “from the firstborn of Pharaoh ... even unto the firstborn of the maidservant” teach?
answers: The plague would affect every social class, from the king to the maidservant
The plague would affect only Pharaoh’s family
The plague would affect only slaves
questions.explanation: The range from Pharaoh to the maidservant emphasizes that every social class in Egypt would be affected.

questions.question: Who is speaking in the words “will I go out into the midst of Egypt”?
answers: Moses
The Lord
Pharaoh
questions.explanation: Moses introduces the message with “Thus saith the Lord,” so “I” refers to the Lord.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the statement “such as there was none like it, nor shall be like it any more”?
answers: The cry would last only a short time
The cry would be heard only in villages
It would be an unprecedented and never-repeated cry
questions.explanation: The repeated comparison emphasizes the extraordinary, unprecedented nature of the event.

easy.question: Who would come down to Moses and bow before him?
answers: All Pharaoh’s servants
All the Israelites
All the Egyptians
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And all these thy servants shall come down unto me, and bow down themselves unto me.”

easy.question: What would Pharaoh’s servants say to Moses?
answers: Return to Pharaoh
Go out, you and all the people who follow you
Stay in Egypt
easy.explanation: Pharaoh’s servants would tell Moses to leave with all the people who followed him.

easy.question: How did Moses leave Pharaoh?
answers: With great joy
Quietly and peacefully
In great anger
easy.explanation: The verse ends by saying that Moses went out from Pharaoh in great anger.

medium.question: What sequence of events is described in the verse?
answers: Pharaoh’s servants bow to Moses, ask him to leave, and then Moses goes out
Moses leaves, and afterward Pharaoh’s servants bow to him
The Israelites bow to Pharaoh, and then Moses remains in Egypt
medium.explanation: First the servants bow, then they tell Moses to leave, and afterward he goes out.

medium.question: What does “in a great anger” mean in the context of Moses leaving Pharaoh?
answers: In great fear
In great anger
In great weariness
medium.explanation: The phrase describes Moses’ strong anger as he left Pharaoh.

medium.question: Why would Pharaoh’s servants tell Moses to leave?
answers: So that Moses and all the people would leave Egypt
So that Moses would rule Egypt
So that Moses would remain alone with Pharaoh
medium.explanation: They tell him, “Go out, you and all the people who follow you.”

challenge.question: Who is meant by “all the people that follow thee”?
answers: The people under Moses’ leadership
Pharaoh’s servants standing near Moses
The Egyptians following Pharaoh
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to the people who followed Moses and were under his leadership.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that Pharaoh’s servants would bow to Moses?
answers: They acknowledged the power and importance of his demand to leave
They wanted Moses to work for Pharaoh
They intended to punish the Israelites
challenge.explanation: Their bowing and request that Moses leave indicate submission to the pressure and demand involving Moses and the people.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “after that I will go out” emphasize?
answers: Moses would leave only after Pharaoh’s servants asked him to
Moses never intended to leave
The people would leave before Moses
challenge.explanation: Moses says, “after that I will go out,” presenting his departure as the stage after the servants’ request.

questions.question: Who is meant by “all the people that follow thee”?
answers: The people under Moses’ leadership
Pharaoh’s servants standing near Moses
The Egyptians following Pharaoh
questions.explanation: The phrase refers to the people who followed Moses and were under his leadership.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that Pharaoh’s servants would bow to Moses?
answers: They acknowledged the power and importance of his demand to leave
They wanted Moses to work for Pharaoh
They intended to punish the Israelites
questions.explanation: Their bowing and request that Moses leave indicate submission to the pressure and demand involving Moses and the people.

questions.question: What does the phrase “after that I will go out” emphasize?
answers: Moses would leave only after Pharaoh’s servants asked him to
Moses never intended to leave
The people would leave before Moses
questions.explanation: Moses says, “after that I will go out,” presenting his departure as the stage after the servants’ request.

paragraphs.title: Pharaoh’s Heart Is Hardened and the Wonders Increase

easy.question: Who told Moses that Pharaoh would not listen to him?
answers: The Lord
Pharaoh
Aaron
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And the Lord said unto Moses.”

easy.question: Who performed all the wonders before Pharaoh?
answers: Moses and the Israelites
Moses and Aaron
Aaron and Pharaoh
easy.explanation: The passage says, “And Moses and Aaron did all these wonders before Pharaoh.”

easy.question: What did Pharaoh not do at the end of the passage?
answers: Speak with Moses
See the wonders
Let the Israelites go out of his land
easy.explanation: The passage ends by saying that Pharaoh would not let the Israelites leave his land.

medium.question: Why would Pharaoh not listen to Moses and Aaron?
answers: So that the Lord’s wonders would be multiplied in Egypt
Because Moses had fled from Egypt
Because the Israelites wanted to remain
medium.explanation: The Lord says that Pharaoh would not listen so that His wonders would be multiplied in the land of Egypt.

medium.question: What happened after Moses and Aaron performed the wonders before Pharaoh?
answers: The Israelites left immediately
The Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart
Pharaoh thanked Moses
medium.explanation: After the wonders are described, the passage says that the Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart, so he did not let the Israelites go.

medium.question: What are “wonders” in the context of this passage?
answers: Laws
Songs
Signs and miracles
medium.explanation: “Wonders” means signs and miracles performed before Pharaoh to display the Lord’s power.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from Pharaoh seeing the wonders and still refusing to let the Israelites go?
answers: Seeing the wonders did not immediately cause Pharaoh to change his decision
Pharaoh was not in Egypt
Moses and Aaron did not perform the wonders
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes that even after the wonders, Pharaoh did not release the Israelites.

challenge.question: What is the relationship between the Lord’s words in verse 9 and the events in verse 10?
answers: Verse 10 cancels verse 9
Verse 10 describes the fulfillment of the Lord’s words: Pharaoh did not listen despite the wonders
Verse 10 describes an event unrelated to Pharaoh
challenge.explanation: Verse 9 says that Pharaoh would not listen, and verse 10 describes him refusing to let the Israelites go.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “out of his land” indicate about where the Israelites were to go?
answers: They would leave only Pharaoh’s palace
They would move from one Egyptian city to another
They were to leave the whole land of Egypt
challenge.explanation: “His land” refers to the territory under Pharaoh’s rule, so the Israelites were to leave Egypt as a whole, not merely one place.

questions.question: What can be inferred from Pharaoh seeing the wonders and still refusing to let the Israelites go?
answers: Seeing the wonders did not immediately cause Pharaoh to change his decision
Pharaoh was not in Egypt
Moses and Aaron did not perform the wonders
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes that even after the wonders, Pharaoh did not release the Israelites.

questions.question: What is the relationship between the Lord’s words in verse 9 and the events in verse 10?
answers: Verse 10 cancels verse 9
Verse 10 describes the fulfillment of the Lord’s words: Pharaoh did not listen despite the wonders
Verse 10 describes an event unrelated to Pharaoh
questions.explanation: Verse 9 says that Pharaoh would not listen, and verse 10 describes him refusing to let the Israelites go.

answers: They would leave only Pharaoh’s palace
They would move from one Egyptian city to another
They were to leave the whole land of Egypt
questions.explanation: “His land” refers to the territory under Pharaoh’s rule, so the Israelites were to leave Egypt as a whole, not merely one place.
